subject: FinEdge privacy onboarding — DPA scope, subprocessor disclosure & signing path
messages:
From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@finedge.com>

Cc: Raj Mehta <raj.m@finedge.com>, FinEdge Legal <legal@finedge.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood DPA + subprocessors — onboarding request

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We're moving FinEdge's integration into pilot next month and legal is accelerating the privacy checklist. Can you share Redwood's current DPA and your subprocessors matrix? Two specific asks from our side: (1) confirmation of EU->US transfer mechanism (SCCs or other), and (2) whether you use any caching/CDN vendors that will see PII tokens in plaintext.

Also, what signing options do you support — DocuSign or AdobeSign? If you can send a template and a one-page summary of your subprocessor categories we can circulate it internally.

Appreciate it — Olivia

Olivia Park
Head of Integrations, FinEdge
olivia.park@finedge.com
+1 415-555-0198

Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA + subprocessors — onboarding request

Hi Olivia — great to hear the pilot timing.

Attaching our standard DPA and a current subprocessor matrix (see attachments: Redwood_DPA_template_v2026-11-15.docx, subprocessors_matrix.xlsx). Quick answers inline:
- EU->US transfer: we can rely on EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) for the processing activity; we also support customer-managed KMS where required (we'll need to map key ownership in the onboarding checklist).
- Caching/CDN: we operate an internal KV cache and use FastEdge CDN for static assets only; FastEdge does not receive plaintext model inputs. The subprocessors matrix includes the short descriptions and categories.

Signing: we support DocuSign (preferred) and AdobeSign. We can send the DPA via DocuSign once you confirm the redline path.

Questions for you:
1) Do you require an explicit prior notice period for adding new subprocessors?
2) Any mandatory contract language from FinEdge legal we should expect beyond the DPA (e.g., minimum liability caps, deletion timelines)?

I'll loop in Laura from Legal and Karthik from Sales for commercial alignment. Next step internally: review FinEdge redlines and propose a signing timeline.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Privacy & Compliance (on the onboarding squad)
Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com

Looping in Marcus for a quick security sanity check, and Laura for legal posture. From a go-to-market perspective, FinEdge is a typical mid-market customer — they are asking for SCCs and will ask for a short notice period on subprocessors. Proposal: offer a 30-day prior notice for new subprocessors plus an opportunity to object for critical categories (security, logging). For signing, DocuSign is fine — we can pre-fill commercial fields and push the envelope once legal confirms the redlines.

If Legal is OK with 30 days and our standard liability cap, I can commit to sending the DocuSign envelope on Thursday to align with their pilot start.

-Karthik

Subject: RE: Redwood DPA + subprocessors — onboarding request

Stephanie — thanks for the quick response and the templates. Please find attached FinEdge's initial redline (FinEdge_DPA_redline_v1.docx) and a couple of clarifying notes:
1) We typically require a 60-day notice for adding certain categories of subprocessors (analytics, profiling). Is Redwood open to 60 days for those categories and 30 days for non-sensitive categories?
2) For EU->US transfers, FinEdge legal prefers SCCs plus a technical control (customer key management when possible). Can you confirm whether customer-managed KMS is supported at the pilot stage?
3) We flagged FastEdge as a potential concern — can Redwood confirm that model prompt text is not forwarded to third-party cache nodes in plaintext (we saw the subprocessors matrix but need explicit confirmation).

Finally, we prefer DocuSign but will accept AdobeSign if needed. We can route the redline through DocuSign or, if you prefer, you can import our redline and send the envelope.

Regards,
Raj Mehta
Director, Procurement & Risk, FinEdge
Attachment stub: FinEdge_DPA_redline_v1.docx
From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Raj Mehta <raj.m@finedge.com>, Olivia Park <olivia.park@finedge.com>

Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA + subprocessors — onboarding request

Thanks Raj — received the redline and the questions. Quick answers and next steps: 

- Notice period: Legal is willing to accept a split approach: 60 days for analytics/profiling vendors, 30 days for infrastructure/CDN vendors. We'll add a short notice schedule to section 4 and capture the categories in the subprocessor appendix.
- KMS: we support customer-managed KMS (BYOK) for Dedicated and Private deployments; for Hosted pilot we can offer envelope-level encryption and a documented roadmap to full BYOK—will note this as an implementation commitment in the MPA.
- Caching/CDN: Marcus confirmed that model prompt text is never written to FastEdge cache nodes in plaintext; the cache stores tokenized and encrypted chunks and is only accessible by Redwood's serving runtime. We'll include a brief attestation in the DPA appendix and provide the relevant SOC2 control IDs.

Proposed execution path:
1) Redwood imports FinEdge redline into our DocuSign envelope (we will not accept the redline as decisive; we'll propose targeted edits in the DocuSign draft).
2) Legal (Laura) and Security (Marcus) will add the short attestation and the SCCs clause.
3) Karthik will send the DocuSign envelope to Olivia/Raj on Monday (23 Nov) if there are no additional commercial asks.

Action items for FinEdge: please confirm you accept the split notice window (60/30) and confirm DocuSign as the signing platform. Once we have that, we'll push the envelope and add the attachment link to the DocuSign package.

I'll attach the updated DPA when Laura finishes the attestation. Thanks all — Stephanie

Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
